newsitem.title: USA: U.S. officials say Fla. drug rings dismantled.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials say Fla. drug rings dismantled.

text.p: The Federal Bureau of Investigation said on Wednesday law officers had dismantled two south Florida drug rings and seized almost 2,000 pounds (900 kg) of cocaine worth about $13.5 million wholesale.

The investigation by the FBI, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration and the U.S. Customs Service led to five arrests, breaking up two groups of Miami area residents who represented major drug suppliers on the north coast of Colombia.
Paul Philip, Special Agent In Charge of the Miami FBI office, said the shipments of cocaine seized in the Miami area were welded into the walls and doors of oceangoing containers.

The FBI said they were seeking a sixth man in connection with the drug rings. They said the five men arrested were working for a group of Colombian smugglers headed by Julio Annicharico and Alberto Orlando Gamboa, who have been indicted for cocaine importing charges by a Florida grand jury.

The FBI also said that cocaine in identically sealed containers was seized recently in Beirut, Lebanon, and Genoa, Italy. Those seizures, of 240 pounds (105 kg) and 1,440 pounds (640 kg), respectively, led to the arrests of at least 14 people and were still being investigated.
